output.brief: First-contact resolution fell mainly because of the 14 April Finance change. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25, and bigger cases now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% that week. Referred calls resolve at about 34%, against 82% for the rest, and those rates did not change. That shift alone explains most of the drop. The new starters are not the cause: their referral rate matches tenured agents, and tenured agents fell by the same amount. The IVR redesign, the tariff rise and workload don't fit the data. Non-referred FCR is flat, and tariff calls still resolve at 85%. I'm fairly confident, though the link to complaints is unproven. Next step: don't put new starters on performance plans. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling of credits. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and the unsupported-credit rate, and widen it only if unsupported credits stay under 1% of value. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. Ask MI for the quick team-level breakdown rather than a three-month dashboard rebuild.
